findings.claim: Removing the constructor means `new UnknownCauseError(cause)` now falls through to the implicit `constructor(...args) { super(...args) }`, so `Error`'s first parameter receives the raw object and `message` becomes `String(cause)` (typically `"[object Object]"`) instead of `cause.message`.
findings.rationale: The rest of the file (not shown in this hunk) still contains `getCauseFromUnknown`, which historically did `return new UnknownCauseError(cause)`. Unless that call site was updated in another hunk to build the error and copy `message`/properties manually, error messages for non-Error causes silently regress from the useful `cause.message` to `[object Object]`. Fairly confident this is a real behavior change worth verifying against the call site.

findings.claim: Dropping `Object.assign(this, cause)` means the arbitrary properties of the unknown cause are no longer copied onto the resulting error, so the index signature `[key: string]: unknown` no longer has anything populating it.
findings.rationale: Consumers (error formatters, logging, `shouldn't-be-lost` fields like `code`/`name` on thrown plain objects) previously saw those fields on the error instance. If the copying isn't reintroduced at the call site, this is a data-loss behavior change for existing callers. The remaining index signature strongly suggests the copy is still expected to happen somewhere.

findings.claim: `getMessage` is deleted; if any other code in this file (or re-export) still referenced it, this is a compile error, and in any case the `'message' in cause` guarded `String(...)` coercion logic is lost.
findings.rationale: Only the first 23 lines are visible, so I can't confirm there are no other references. The guarded coercion also handled the case where `cause.message` is a non-string (symbol/object) safely; naive replacements elsewhere may not. Moderate confidence — worth checking the full file compiles and that message derivation was reimplemented.

findings.claim: With no explicit constructor, `UnknownCauseError` no longer sets a distinguishing `message`, and TypeScript will now type-check `new UnknownCauseError(x)` against `ErrorConstructor` (`message?: string, options?: ErrorOptions`), so passing an `object` will be a type error rather than a silently accepted cause.
findings.rationale: This is the type-level counterpart of the runtime issue: previously the constructor accepted `object`. Any remaining `new UnknownCauseError(someObject)` will fail to compile under the built-in Error signature. Reporting in case the call site was only partially migrated.
